draft.title: Excise and import duties
card: a tax on certain goods made in Australia, such as fuel, alcohol and tobacco. It is added to the price the buyer pays.
a tax on goods brought in from overseas. It is paid when the goods enter the country, and it is also passed on to the buyer.
Both taxes raise the price of the goods they apply to. A higher price can lead some people to buy less, or to choose a different product.
Both also raise money for the government. An import duty can make imported goods cost more than similar goods made in Australia.
draft.remember: Excise taxes some local goods and import duties tax overseas goods. Both lift prices.

a.q: Which of these is an import duty?
opts: A tax on shoes made overseas and sold in Australia
A tax on petrol made and sold in Australia
A tax on a new house sold in Australia
A tax on the wages earned by a worker in Australia
a.why: An import duty is charged on goods that come in from overseas, so it applies to the shoes. A tax on petrol made here is an excise, which is the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: Where do the taxed goods come from?

b.q: The government raises the excise on cigarettes made in Australia. What is the most likely effect on the price and on what people buy?
opts: The price rises and some people buy fewer cigarettes
The price falls and some people buy more cigarettes
The price rises and nobody changes what they buy
The price stays the same and people buy fewer
b.why: Excise is passed on to buyers, so the price goes up. A higher price can lead some people to buy less. It does not force everyone to change, but it can change some choices.
b.clue: What does a tax do to the price?

a.best: A tax on shoes made overseas and sold in Australia

b.best: The price rises and some people buy fewer cigarettes
